extracted.intended_audience: recording artists, producers, engineers, record labels, music supervisors, and Recording Academy entrants/submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Official Recording Academy rules and guidelines describing eligibility, category definitions, crediting, submission requirements, and judging criteria for GRAMMY Awards entries for the 68th GRAMMY Awards year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Period
rubrics_metrics.description: The 68th GRAMMY Awards eligibility period is August 31, 2024 - August 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings must be released during the eligibility period and be commercially released, nationally distributed and available from any date within the eligibility period through at least the date of the current year’s Final Round voting deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Recordings (definition and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: "New recordings" is defined as material that has been recorded within five years of the release date and not previously released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings not newly recorded are eligible only in specified categories (e.g., Best Historical Album; Best Compilation Soundtrack Album; Best Immersive Audio Album if the multichannel mix is new; Best Remixed Recording if the remix is new; Best Recording Package if package is new; Best Album Cover/Notes if new), and certain classical multidisc sets have additional exceptions when 100% previously unreleased material and single artist/composer conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: "General distribution" is defined as the broad release of a recording, available nationwide via streaming services, brick-and-mortar stores and/or third-party online retailers. (Imports are not eligible.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streaming services are defined as paid subscription, full catalog, on-demand streaming/limited download services that have existed in the U.S. for at least one full year as of the entry deadline. Spoken word albums have exceptions (SoundCloud and e-reader links allowed). All recordings entered must have an assigned ISRC or UPC number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Recordings (copyright compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings must be non-infringing, original works of authorship; if a recording embodies third-party copyrighted work, appropriate authorization must have been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allegations arise that a recording is unauthorized, the Academy will consider the allegations and determine eligibility in its sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative Artificial Intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Only human creators are eligible to be submitted for consideration for, nominated for, or win a GRAMMY Award. A work that contains no human authorship is not eligible in any categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that include AI-generated material are eligible only if (1) the human authorship component is meaningful and more than de minimis, (2) the human authorship is relevant to the category entered (e.g., songwriting categories require meaningful human authorship in music/lyrics), and (3) authors of AI material are not eligible to be nominees/recipients for their AI contribution. 'De minimis' is defined as lacking significance or importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singles and Tracks (definitions and cross-year eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single is a song or instrumental released separately from an album; a track is an individual song or instrumental released as part of an album. They are judged identically in Categories where both are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks/singles from a previous year's album may be eligible in many genre fields provided they were not entered previously and the album did not win a performance Category; tracks from albums released previously are ineligible in certain categories (e.g., Best Instrumental Composition, Arranging categories, Song Written For Visual Media, Remixed Recording, Songwriter Of The Year Non-Classical, Producer Of The Year, and all Classical categories). A single or track is eligible in one specialized Genre Field but may be screened into one field while its album is screened into another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Albums (definition and new-material thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: An album is a collection of audio recordings issued for sale, download or streaming as a unit. To qualify as an album, a release must contain at least five tracks and total at least 15 minutes, or any number of tracks if total playing time is at least 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Albums must contain greater than 75% playing time of newly recorded (within five years), previously unreleased recordings. To be eligible in a specific Genre Category, an album must contain greater than 50% playing time of that genre. Singles released during current or previous eligibility periods have specific rules about counting against 'new recordings' thresholds (they may be excluded in certain situations). Updated/revised/expanded versions of previously submitted albums are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songs (songwriting eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A song must comprise music and lyrics to be eligible in a songwriting category (melody qualifies as music) and must have been released on an eligible recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible in songwriting categories (subject to sampled-writer ineligibility for awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured Artists (crediting and recognition thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized as a GRAMMY nominee, a featured artist or collaborator must be credited as an artist or featured artist and make a significant and artistic contribution beyond accompaniment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured artists are GRAMMY-eligible in genre album categories if they perform greater than 50% of playing time; eligible in performance categories if credited as a featured artist on the track/single. Featured artists who perform under 50% of a winning album’s playing time receive an Achievement Certificate. An album credited to one artist with many guest artists may be considered a 'Various Artists' album at the Academy’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampled and Interpolated Material
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample is an element of a previously released recording incorporated into a new recording (entire parts or isolated sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings featuring samples/interpolations are eligible in performance categories only if the performance up for consideration is newly recorded per Academy definitions. Recordings featuring samples are eligible in songwriting categories; however, writers of sampled or interpolated material are not eligible to be nominees or GRAMMY recipients for the portion consisting of such sampled material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Mixes and Remixes (single-version rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one version/mix of a recording is eligible in the GRAMMY process in any year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different versions are released in the same eligibility year, the label releasing the original artist’s version decides which mix to enter (provided it is otherwise eligible). In Best Song Written For Visual Media, the film/soundtrack version may be entered even if different from versions entered elsewhere. Current remixes or new mixes of recordings released in a previous awards year are generally only eligible in Best Remixed Recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song Lyrics and Album Notes in Translation
rubrics_metrics.description: For lyrics or album notes originally written in one language and translated/adapted into another, the original writer is always the eligible writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Disqualification for Incorrect/Incomplete Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy reserves the right to disqualify entries without liability if information is incorrect or incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy may also disqualify entries if signers fail to provide required streaming links by the end of the eligibility period or fail to send required product for craft entries by listed due dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Deadline and Payment Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have not submitted and/or submitted payment for all entries by the OEP deadline (August 29, 2025), your entries will not be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Enforcement and Rule Violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy may disqualify any entry, and revoke any nomination or GRAMMY Award, if it discovers that the corresponding entry was submitted in violation of the Academy’s Rules and Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy may also disqualify entries for violations of Voting And Solicitation Guidelines or For Your Consideration (FYC) guidelines on member websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Category Placement and Eligibility Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy has the right to place any selection into the Category it deems appropriate and to pass on the eligibility of any selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy may designate classification of achievement (performing, songwriting, producing, etc.) and make the final determination of the persons entitled to awards recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Award Entitlement Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the Academy’s policy that the GRAMMY be awarded to the person who, at the Academy’s sole discretion, is properly entitled to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Replace Track Entries by Album
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy may replace track entries by an entry for the entire album if several tracks by the same artist, totaling greater than 50% of the album’s playing time, are accepted in the same category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Withdraw or Consolidate Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy may withdraw any category in any one year if it determines there is an insufficient number of entries and, at its discretion, place affected entries in one or more other categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Disqualify Excessive Entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy reserves the right to disqualify without liability what it considers excessive entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Protecting Voting Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy may take whatever measures it deems necessary to protect the integrity of the GRAMMY Awards from outside influence, bloc voting or other factors that could jeopardize the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Inappropriate Entry Errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recording is entered inappropriately, and if the error in entering is not discovered by the Recording Academy before the First Ballot, the entry will be disqualified from the process without any liability for further action from the Recording Academy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Judging Copies and Craft Entries Liability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy assumes no liability with respect to Craft entries if the required judging copies for Nominating Committees fail to reach the Academy by the due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy Rights: Human Creators Only (reiteration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only human creators are eligible to be submitted for consideration for, nominated for, or win a GRAMMY Award; the Academy may disqualify an entry lacking meaningful and more than de minimis human authorship relevant to the entered category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De minimis is defined as lacking significance or importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Of The Year: Evaluation Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings entered for consideration should represent the best overall achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements to be considered are performance, production and engineering; secondary elements are songwriting/composition, arranging and performance of backup vocalists and musicians, as applicable. Nominees include Artist(s), Producer(s), Engineer(s), Mixer(s), Mastering Engineer(s) if other than Artist(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Of The Year: Evaluation Elements and Nominee Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Albums entered should represent the best overall achievement by the performer(s), album producer(s), engineer(s)/mixer(s), and songwriter(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other elements considered include arranging and musicianship. Nominees are Artist(s), Featured Artist(s), Songwriter(s) of new material, Producer(s), Recording Engineer(s), Mixer(s) & Mastering Engineer(s) with greater than 20% playing time on the album. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to those with greater than 20% playing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song Of The Year: Songwriting Award Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Songs should represent the best achievement in songwriting. Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A song must comprise music and lyrics to be eligible and must have been released on a recording for the first time, or achieved prominence for the first time, during the current eligibility period. Nominees and statuettes awarded to Songwriter(s) of new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist: Breakthrough & Release Minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes an artist whose eligibility-period release(s) achieved a breakthrough into the public consciousness and notably impacted the musical landscape; primary element considered is the artist’s performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum releases to meet eligibility: five singles/tracks or one album. Production elements should not be considered. Screening Committees determine whether an artist had attained breakthrough or prominence prior to the eligibility year (which would result in disqualification). An artist may not enter this Category more than three times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist: Eligibility/Ineligibility Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists who is eligible and not eligible for Best New Artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible: solo artists and established duos/groups, solo artists formerly with duos/groups (if the duo/group had not attained prominence), new established duos/groups of former solo artists (provided none had attained prominence), new recording artists from other disciplines. Not eligible: any artist who had achieved a breakthrough in a prior eligibility period; any artist with a previous GRAMMY nomination as a performer; collaborations of individuals not an established group; artists credited only as featured artists; choirs/large ensembles of 16+ members; non-music-performing video performers; musical craftspeople; persons active in public life whose recording was not intended as a commercial release; groups continuing the name/tradition of an ineligible previous group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical: Body-of-Work Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in production of non-classical audio recordings for a producer whose body of work released during the eligibility year represents consistently outstanding creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One album OR six tracks/singles constitute the minimum to be eligible. The body of work will be up to nine projects (producer chooses which nine if more are submitted). Each producer must provide at least one eligible single/track producing an artist other than themselves. Production teams must enter projects they worked on as a team; an individual cannot appear on the ballot both as an individual and as a member of a producer team. Only recordings released in the current eligibility year are eligible; tracks from albums released in a previous year are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical: Body-of-Work Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes written excellence in songwriting for songwriters whose body of work released for the first time during the eligibility year represents artistic excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Songwriters must have written a minimum of four songs in which they are credited as a songwriter. Songs where the songwriter is also credited as a Primary or Featured Artist or Producer do not qualify to satisfy the minimum song threshold. Songwriters may enter up to five more songs that include additional credits (max nine). If over nine titles are entered, the songwriter or representative determines which songs appear on the ballot. Songs from albums released in a previous year are not eligible; rereleased, covered, remixed, reissued, and historical recordings are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance/Electronic Recording: Genre and New-Material Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in recordings from established Dance and Electronic genres; Category is open to recordings specifically and originally targeted to the Dance and/or Electronic market with significant electronic-based instrumentation generally based around a rhythmic dance beat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings MUST contain greater than 50% new material. If vocals or any significant part of the music have not been recorded within the last five years or were released prior to the current year’s eligibility period, it can only be entered in Best Remixed Recording. Dance remixes are eligible in Best Remixed Recording only and may not be entered in Best Dance/Electronic Recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance Pop Recording: Genre Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in dance recordings rooted in electronic and club-oriented production while incorporating elements of pop songwriting and vocals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible recordings showcase fundamentals of dance music: rhythmic momentum, dynamic build-ups and breakdowns, and instrumental-driven energy shifts that define the genre. Dance remixes are eligible only in Best Remixed Recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Remixed Recording: Remixer's Award Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in remixed recordings where the remixer takes previously recorded/released material and creatively adds to, alters or transforms it to create a new and unique performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not for covers, re-recordings, remastered releases, or edits that are only shortened versions. Addition of a vocal by a featured artist without substantive change to the original music recording is not eligible as a remix. Singles/tracks need not be commercially released if released to clubs or radio in the U.S. for the first time during the eligibility year. The original recording being remixed does not have to have been released during the current eligibility period—only the remixed recording must be released during the current eligibility year. Only one version/mix of a recording is eligible in most Categories in any year. Both the remixed version and original must be available to the Academy for judging purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Producer Credits (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines eligible producer credits and their duties: Producer, Co-Producer, Vocal Production/Vocals Produced By, 'Featured Artist' Produced By, Compilation Producer (eligible only for specific categories), Immersive Audio Producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producer duties include overall creative/technical oversight, overseeing sessions, making creative decisions, selecting final takes, participating in song selection, overseeing staffing/budgets/schedules and supplying accurate crediting information. Co-producer makes significant contributions. Vocal producers have control over vocal recording sessions. Compilation producers have primary responsibility for track selection on compilation or historical albums. Immersive audio producer same as producer but for immersive formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Eligible Producer Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists producer-type credits that are not eligible for GRAMMY recognition as producers: Executive Producer, Assistant/Associate Producer, Additional Production, Strings (or other instrument) Produced By, Produced On Behalf Of (the content owner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These roles are typically supervisory, administrative, partial, or not responsible for day-to-day creative oversight and thus not eligible as 'producer' credits for awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Engineer Credits (definitions and special cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines eligible engineer credits: Engineer, Recording Engineer/Recorded By, Mixed By/Mixer/Mix Engineer, Remix Engineer/Remixer (for Best Remixed Recording only), Vocals Recorded/Engineered By, Balance Engineer (classical), Mastering Engineer (eligible only in certain categories), Tonmeister (classical requirement), Restoration Engineer (Best Historical Album only), Immersive Audio Engineer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineers are actively responsible for creative recording/mixing decisions and technical issues. Mastering engineers are only eligible for statuettes in select categories (Best Historical Album; Best Immersive Audio Album; Best Engineered Album Classical; Best Engineered Album Non-Classical; Record Of The Year; Album Of The Year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Eligible Engineer Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists engineering credits not eligible for awards: Pro Tools Engineer/DAW Engineer, Pro Tools Operator, Pro Tools Editor/DAW Editor, Additional Pro Tools/DAW Engineer, Engineer For Mix, Assistant/Second Engineer, Additional Engineer, Assistant Mix Engineer/Mix Assistant, Mix Programming, Digital Editing, Digital Engineering/Programming, DSD Recording roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These roles are generally technical/operational and not considered to have sufficient aesthetic contribution to merit an engineer award/credit in most categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Supervisor Definition and Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Music Supervisor identifies, secures and supervises all music-related talent; liaises/negotiates with representation; possesses knowledge of costs and budgets; determines feasibility of schedules; delivers required music elements consistent with technical requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also manages/securing legal rights of recordings, clearances of synchronization and master use licenses, credits, cue sheets, and determines viability/creation/securing of ancillary products (soundtracks, singles, videos, downloads) for promotion or revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-Edition Releases Distribution Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited-edition releases do not meet the distribution requirement for eligibility in most categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution eligibility is based on an artist’s typical shipment policies. The Academy may inquire with the manufacturer about the number of recordings normally shipped and may determine eligibility if shipment is substantially less than normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Recordings Submission Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering and Producer entries require submission of a lossless streaming link. If not available, the original digital file must have quality comparable to at least 16-bit/44.1 kHz and 44 kHz/16-bit audio for certain engineering categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of label credits (producers, mixers, songwriters, etc.) must be included in the required metadata file. Any requested documentation (including list of retailers/streaming services) must be provided if requested by the Academy to verify crediting or release date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voices Used As 'Instruments' (ineligibility as instrumental performances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocal performances are never eligible as instrumental performances, regardless of method of vocal production (scatting, beatboxing, throat singing, vocally mimicking instruments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy or GRAMMY Telecast Recordings Ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings released by the Recording Academy or affiliate-produced releases, including performances from GRAMMY Awards Telecasts, are not eligible in the awards process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playback Systems (specialized equipment ineligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: If specialized equipment is needed to play a recording (other than common consumer devices), the recording is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Pianocorder cassettes not eligible because they only play back on a Pianocorder Reproducing System retrofit onto a piano.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings Made Of Playback Systems Using Previously Recorded Performances
rubrics_metrics.description: A new recording that records a device playing a previously recorded performance (e.g., piano rolls, player piano systems, Zenph, Welte-Mignon) is not eligible in the Best Historical Album Category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These playback-system recordings are only eligible in Best Engineered Album, where the new recording of the playback would be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry List—Type/Font Treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants are allowed special characters and unusual typographical treatments in artist names and titles on ballot entry lists, so long as characters may be found on a computer keyboard or through standard diacritical markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Merit Awards: Lifetime Achievement Award Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented by vote of the Recording Academy’s National Trustees to performers who, during their lifetimes, have made creative contributions of outstanding artistic significance to the field of recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information including past honorees is available from the Academy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Merit Awards: Trustees Award Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented by vote of the National Trustees to individuals who have made significant contributions, other than performance, to the field of recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Merit Awards: Technical GRAMMY Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented by vote of the Producers & Engineers Wing Advisory Council and Chapter Committees and ratification by the National Trustees to individuals/companies/institutions who have made contributions of outstanding technical significance to the recording field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harry Belafonte Best Song For Social Change Award Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A CEO’s Merit Award to honor songwriter(s) of message-driven music that speaks to social issues and has demonstrated and inspired positive global impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients selected annually by a committee of peers dedicated to artistic expression and songwriting craft; refreshed language welcomes single and multi-movement compositions containing lyrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Educator Award Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes current educators (K–college, public and private) who have made significant and lasting contributions to music education and demonstrate commitment to maintaining music education in schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information and past recipients available from the Academy/GRAMMY Museum.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRAMMY Hall Of Fame Induction Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors recordings of lasting qualitative or historical significance that are at least 25 years old, selected annually by a special member committee of eminent professionals from all branches of the recording arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information including list of Hall Of Fame recordings is available from the Academy.
